Task Name: Consolidated PR #99 (Universal backend data sanitization & boundary limits) into this branch and fixed its app-breaking bug. Task Name: Phase 6: closed a HIGH-severity price-tampering hole on the guest booking page. Audit found the payment layer is solid (Razorpay order + /verify always charge server booking.total_amount, webhook HMAC verified), so the only lever was booking creation. create_public_booking trusted CLIENT-submitted values for the final charge: (a) add-on prices were summed straight from the request (PublicAddOn.price) with NO catalog lookup and no ge=0 bound -> a guest could send a negative/understated add-on price (e.g. -10000) and drive total_amount below the room cost, i.e. pay ~Rs.1 for a Rs.10k room; the per-room 1% tolerance check did not cover add-ons at all. (b) room subtotal/tax used the client total_price + price_per_night, allowing <=1% underpayment and tax-slab evasion (send price_per_night=999 to hit the 0% slab). Fix: add-on prices are now looked up server-side from the addons table (by id+hotel_id+is_active), unknown/inactive add-ons are rejected (400); rooms now charge from the SERVER-recomputed total and resolve the tax slab from the server nightly price; total_amount clamped to >=0; defense-in-depth ge=0 bounds added to PublicAddOn.price and PublicRoomBooking price fields + guests ge=1/le=50. Added TestAddOnPriceIntegrity (tampered low price uses catalog price; negative price -> 422; unknown add-on -> 400).
API Calls Count: create_public_booking now issues 1 extra bounded query (SELECT addons WHERE id IN(...) AND hotel_id AND is_active) only when add-ons are present; no change to the room/availability queries; payment endpoints unchanged
Caching & Database Details: Reads addons catalog (indexed on hotel_id) for server-side price; no schema/DB migration; booking.addons now stores server-verified prices
Security Controls / IDOR Prevention: Server-authoritative pricing: add-on + room amounts and tax slab are recomputed server-side and never trust the client; negative/understated/unknown values rejected; total can never go negative; payment still charges server total_amount with signature+amount cross-check

Task Name: Phase 7: fixed a SEV-1 broken-import bug that silently broke ALL online payment confirmation. payments.py used `from app.api.v1.public.bookings import _update_guest_loyalty` in two places (the /razorpay/verify handler and the /razorpay/webhook handler) but that module does not exist (ModuleNotFoundError; the helper lives in app.guest_booking._booking_helpers). The webhook path crashed the same way (500 -> Razorpay retries fail). No test caught it because no e2e test exercised a valid-signature confirmation. Grepped the codebase for other app.api.v1.public / app.api imports — none remain. Added TestOnlinePaymentVerifyConfirms (mocks the Razorpay client so signature+amount checks pass and asserts the booking flips to CONFIRMED with paid_amount set) as a regression guard. Also audited the rest of the money/attack surface: create-order, /verify amount+signature+receipt cross-check, webhook HMAC + replay protection + amount backstop, and cancellation/refund (email-gated, refund server-computed & capped at paid_amount, no auto payout) — all found sound.

Task Name: Phase 8: storage lifecycle / orphaned-media cleanup (storage audit). Previously deleting a room or hotel left all its uploaded images in the public hotel-assets Supabase bucket forever (storage cost + abuse surface). Added app/core/storage.py with a best-effort, never-raises cleanup helper: extract_object_path() only resolves object paths INSIDE our own hotel-assets bucket (foreign hosts / other buckets / non-strings return None, so a tampered URL can't make us delete anything unexpected); collect_object_paths() tolerates unknown media-dict shapes by scanning all string values + de-dupes; delete_media_objects() batches the removal and swallows every error. Wired into delete_room (hotelier) and delete_hotel (super admin): both snapshot media BEFORE the cascade delete and schedule removal via BackgroundTasks so it runs after the response and never blocks/breaks the delete. delete_hotel also snapshots every room's photos before the raw-SQL cascade. Confirmed the upload endpoint is already hardened (auth + 20/hour rate limit + 5MB cap + extension allowlist + magic-byte content-type derivation, PUB-02). Added tests/test_storage_cleanup.py (10 cases: path extraction incl. foreign-host/other-bucket rejection, dict/string collection + dedup, bucket-scoped removal, no-op when empty, never-raises on backend error).
API Calls Count: delete_room + delete_hotel now schedule a background storage-remove for the deleted entity's media; no new request-path latency (runs post-response); upload endpoint unchanged
Caching & Database Details: No DB/schema change; removes orphaned objects from the hotel-assets bucket; cleanup is best-effort and never participates in the DB transaction

Validation parity with images (PUB-02): magic-byte checks reject spoofed files (_looks_like_mp4 = 'ftyp' box at bytes 4-8; _looks_like_webm = EBML header 0x1A45DFA3), so a .mp4 containing <script>/HTML is rejected with 400 and the bucket always serves a correct video/* content-type derived from bytes (not the client header). Separate 100MB cap for video (MAX_VIDEO_SIZE) vs 5MB for images, with an early Content-Length guard before reading the body into memory. Videos go to the public hotel-assets bucket (same as images) so the existing Phase-8 storage cleanup already purges them on room/hotel delete. Auth + 20/hour rate limit unchanged. Added tests/test_video_upload.py (7: valid mp4/webm, fake-mp4 and bad-webm rejection, valid upload via endpoint asserting derived content-type, oversized 413). NOTE: per-entity persistence (a videos JSON column on room_types/hotels via the create_all-safe ALTER pattern), the hotelier upload UI + guest gallery playback, and infra-dependent items (transcoding, CDN, virus scanning) are tracked as follow-ups — not in this slice.
